 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The hype train was in full force about the possibilities of how DeMar DeRozan could fit into the Denver Nuggets' high-powered offense before the season started. But the fit has been trash so far, and the Nuggets need to start rethinking whether they should keep running DeRozan out for more than spot minutes at the rate it's going. But they've got a solution in Cam Whitmore, who's been lighting it up in the G League, if they're willing to try him. Wait, hear me out!
 DeRozan's been a huge disappointment, and he's detrimental to both the Nuggets' offense and defense right now. He can't knock down a three, and he's been bad on his drives to the rim. Sure, he's hitting a mid-range jumper, his bread and butter, here and there. But that's not what the struggling Nuggets offense needs.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Cam Whitmore deserves a shot at some minutes at wing
 The Nuggets assigned the two-way Whitmore to the Grand Rapids Gold of the G League, and through his two games, he's looked impressive . He's averaging 26 points, and he just had a 32-point game, including 5-for-11 from three. Had an impressive alley-oop dunk off a Ryan Nembhard assist, and he showed his outstanding downhill game by getting to the rim on physical drives multiple times. His athleticism and quickness were on full display, and it makes you wonder just how much of a difference his pace would make for the Nuggets.
 DeRozan lacks athletic explosiveness, and he's shoehorned into his midrange game, which messes up the spacing for the Nuggets. Whitmore could at least be a bigger threat from three and draw a defender closer to him.
 Clearly, Whitmore could offer a solution to the DeRozan issues. Whitmore's offense hasn't really been a question since he was drafted with the 20th pick in the first round in 2023 by the Houston Rockets. It's his defense that's been a problem. But really, could he do much worse than DeRozan? It's apples-to-apples on the defensive side, and at least if Whitmore makes a mistake, he's got the athleticism to try and make up for it.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If not Whitmore, Bryce Hopkins needs a chance
 If the Nuggets want to get Whitmore more floor time in the G League for his development, that's fine. But at least give Bryce Hopkins more minutes in DeRozan's spot. Hopkins looked fantastic in the game in which he filled in for DeRozan against the Toronto Raptors. Hopkins had 18 points on 6-for-7 shooting, including some great drives and finishes close to the rim.
 Nuggets head coach David Adelman needs to try one of them over DeRozan in a game soon. DeRozan is having a hard time adjusting to his role. Hopkins did not. Whitmore may not. And all Nikola Jokic wants is for the role players to "do their jobs." Time to stop being stubborn, Adelman, and try something else.
